title: ROMA c. ITALIE ET AUTRES REQUÊTES
summary: In the case of Roma v. Italy and Others, the applicants included Guido Roma and several other individuals, some of whom identified as Roma or Travellers, bringing their claims against the Italian state. The case highlighted the vulnerability of Roma and Traveller communities in Italy, who have historically faced discrimination and obstacles in accessing justice and property rights. The applicants, residing in various Italian cities such as Salerno, Brescia, Palermo, and Milan, lodged their complaints between 2010 and 2011, alleging violations of their rights under the European Convention on Human Rights, specifically concerning fair trial guarantees, effective remedies, and protection of property. The European Court of Human Rights examined the case under Articles 6 (right to a fair trial), 13 (right to an effective remedy), and Article 1 of Protocol No. 1 (protection of property). However, before a full judgment was rendered, the parties reached a friendly settlement, which the Court found to be consistent with respect for human rights. As a result, the Court struck the case from its list in accordance with Article 39 of the Convention. This outcome reflects the ongoing importance of negotiated solutions in addressing the longstanding challenges faced by Roma and Traveller communities in Italy, against a backdrop of persistent marginalisation across Europe.
